newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Another cyclone headed New Zealand's way.
newsitem.headline: Another cyclone headed New Zealand's way.

text.p: Another tropical cyclone is heading New Zealand's way, just 10 days after the upper North Island was lashed by the remains of Cyclone Fergus, forecasters said on Wednesday.

Met Service chief meteorologist Augie Auer told Reuters Cyclone Drena, which has started with more intensity than Fergus, is travelling south east and could hit the north of New Zealand around Friday.
Drena formed recently between Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands, the same area as Fergus. It is currently battering New Caledonia with wind gusts of up to 215 kilometres an hour.

"The latest computer predictions...suggest that a track similar to Fergus of about 10 days ago is not unlikely. We are not positioning it exactly...we're reserving that tweaking to some overnight analysis and early morning analysis," Auer said.

"We are aware of the fact that it's still holiday season here. There are...thousands of people still holidaying and vacationing in some of what could be the hardest hit areas, namely the Bay of Islands, Coromandel and Bay of Plenty, even the Auckland metro area."

Cyclone Fergus was downgraded to a "very deep depression" by the time it reached New Zealand. Although it dumped torrential rain and caused slips and flooding in some areas, Fergus did not live up to many of the MetService's warnings.
Auer said it was important people were not complacent about hearing two cyclone warnings in two weeks.
"I'm urging people: don't turn your back on this sucker."
